dct_description_sm: Thawing permafrost and reduced quality and quantity of surface water available for the drinking water supplies of Inuit communities are among the consequences of global warming already observed in northern regions. Although the influence of melting permafrost on groundwater is still largely unknown, it is anticipated that groundwater recharge will be improved making groundwater resources available as a possible source of drinking water for these northern communities. Groundwater is also generally a cheaper and more reliable source of drinking water than surface water. Hydrogeochemical tracers were used in this study in order to characterize the groundwater flow system in Umiujaq, Nunavik.
dct_title_s: Hydrogeochemistry of groundwater, surface water, permafrost and precipitation in Umiujaq, Nunavik, Qubec
